clue.text: Mates capsized in smack

indicators.note: a boat that has capsized is turned over, so in this down light the word for mates is turned upside down

parts.note: mates are pals, friends

explanation.surface: Shipmates whose boat overturned while they were sailing in a smack, a small fishing boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smack' looks like the fishing boat that capsized, but it is the definition, a blow with the open hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a smack and this are both a sharp blow delivered with the flat of the hand.

clue.text: Fidgeting, sat Right Honourable

indicators.note: fidgeting means moving restlessly, so the letters of sat and right are shuffled about

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Right Honourable member of parliament squirming in their seat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right Honourable' reads as one title, but 'Right' is part of the anagram fodder with 'sat' and 'Honourable' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone straight is honest and upright in dealings, which is what honourable conduct means.

clue.text: Flimsy element

definitions.meaning: a flimsy is a thin sheet of copying paper
a chemical element, atomic number six, the basis of organic life

explanation.surface: Two bare definitions side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: A flimsy was a thin duplicate copy made with carbon paper, and the chemical element is the same word.

clue.text: Left in Aden, bags possibly heading for hilly Asian country

indicators.note: possibly says the letters may be arranged some other way, so the pooled letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its first letter, taken from hilly

explanation.surface: A traveller in Aden with luggage, setting off for a mountainous country in Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges L, ADEN and BAGS into BANGLADES; 'heading for' takes the H of hilly to finish it.
explanation.definitionFit: The South Asian nation bordering India and Myanmar is a country in Asia.

clue.text: Piece of advice given by experienced writer

parts.note: to have experienced a feeling is to have felt it
a tip is a helpful hint or piece of advice

explanation.surface: An old hand at writing passing on a useful hint to a beginner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'writer' looks like a person, but here it is the pen itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a pen with a fibre point is a writing instrument, so a writer in the sense of a thing that writes.

clue.text: Sacrifice, to the advantage of work

parts.note: to be for something is to be in its favour, to its advantage
a machine that works is said to go

explanation.surface: Giving something up because it will benefit one's job.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to sacrifice something is to do without it or give it up voluntarily.

clue.text: Wrote up Peter Pan merrily receiving crown

indicators.note: receiving means one group takes another inside it
merrily suggests the letters of up, Peter and Pan dancing about into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
the crown of something is its top

explanation.surface: J M Barrie's boy hero cheerfully being crowned in a written account.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wrote up' reads as one phrase, but 'up' joins the anagram fodder and 'Wrote' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to set pen to paper is to begin writing, so the phrase stands for wrote.

clue.text: Accumulate a million as head of state

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, here from state

explanation.surface: A national leader piling up a vast personal fortune.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to accumulate is to gather together or pile up a store of something.

clue.text: Colour Zeiss perhaps introduced to series

indicators.note: introduced to means put inside, so the name goes into the word for series

parts.note: a set is a series or collection
Carl Zeiss was the German optician; perhaps marks him as one example of someone so named

explanation.surface: Zeiss lenses being brought in to a range of colour products.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a bright red shade is one kind of colour.

clue.text: Good packaging, reportedly, for brandy

indicators.note: reportedly says we hear the word for packaging spoken, and write down what it sounds like

parts.note: a wrapper is the packaging around a product

explanation.surface: A bottle of Italian spirit well wrapped for a journey.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian spirit distilled from grape pomace is a kind of brandy.

clue.text: Desperately got bag on sledge

indicators.note: desperately suggests wild disorder, so the letters of got, bag and on are thrown about

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone frantically grabbing a bag before jumping onto a sledge.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: this is a long narrow sled used for sliding down snowy slopes.

clue.text: Flier, untrained for battle

parts.note: a flier is something that flies; a goose is one such bird
green means inexperienced or untrained

explanation.surface: An inexperienced pilot being sent into combat.
explanation.walkthrough: Goose Green was a 1982 battle of the Falklands War between British and Argentine forces.
explanation.definitionFit: Proper name: the settlement on East Falkland gave its name to a 1982 land battle.

clue.text: Levy that could make Take That awfully cross?

definitions.text: Levy that could make Take That awfully cross?

parts.words: Levy that could make Take That awfully cross?
parts.note: a hidden levy annoys taxpayers; Take That, the British boy band, had members caught up in a tax avoidance scheme, so a sneaky tax would anger them

explanation.surface: A tax that would infuriate a famous pop group.
explanation.walkthrough: Take That is a British boy band; some members were publicly criticised in 2014 over a tax avoidance scheme. 'awfully cross' teases an anagram, but there is none.
explanation.definitionFit: A levy raised without people noticing, such as a quiet rise in duty, is a hidden form of taxation.

clue.text: Join forces, gathering right away

indicators.note: away says something is taken off, here the letter for right from the gathering

parts.note: a rally is a mass gathering

explanation.surface: Political allies uniting at a rally while the right wing stays away.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to join forces with someone is to unite or side with them.

clue.text: Article by newspaper on personality's fraudulent practice

indicators.note: in an across light, on means placed after, so the article and paper come behind the word for personality

parts.note: one's personality is one's identity
the is the definite article
FT is the Financial Times, a British newspaper

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece exposing a celebrity's crooked dealings.
explanation.walkthrough: The FT, short for the Financial Times, is a British daily newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: stealing someone's personal details to pose as them is a well-known kind of fraud.

clue.text: Understood mischievous child was untruthful

parts.note: an imp is a naughty, mischievous child
to have been untruthful is to have lied

explanation.surface: A naughty youngster was clearly telling fibs.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: what is suggested without being said outright is understood or hinted.

clue.text: The turn involving a cast member

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: involving means wrapping round, so the word for turn holds the a inside

parts.note: a spin is a turn or twirl

explanation.surface: A music-hall turn that features one of the company of actors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn' suggests a stage act, but here it is a spin.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an actor, one of a play's cast, is called by this word after Thespis of ancient Greek drama.

clue.text: Chum after ring and gemstone

indicators.note: after places the word for chum behind the ring shape

parts.note: O is round like a ring
a chum is a pal

explanation.surface: A friend chasing a ring with a precious stone set in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: this milky iridescent mineral is one of the common precious stones.

clue.text: Snake caught constricting flightless bird

indicators.note: constricting means squeezing round something, so the word for caught surrounds the bird

parts.note: copped is slang for caught
the rhea is a large flightless South American bird

explanation.surface: A snake caught squeezing an ostrich-like bird to death.
explanation.walkthrough: 'constricting' fits the snake picture, yet it is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: this venomous North American pit viper is a kind of snake.

clue.text: Rides in circles

definitions.meaning: rides a bicycle, as a verb
a verb meaning goes round and round, revolves

explanation.surface: Two bare definitions side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: One who pedals a bike rides it, and something that turns round repeatedly circles; the verb covers both.

clue.text: Examination of accounts — part of fraud itself

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A check of the books turns out to be a piece of the swindle.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an official inspection of a firm's financial records is what this word names.

clue.text: Fizzy thing — better bedtime drink

indicators.note: fizzy suggests bubbling agitation, so the letters of thing are stirred up

parts.note: taken as written
to cap something is to better or outdo it

explanation.surface: Something sparkling that beats any other drink before bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'better' looks like an adjective, but it is the verb to outdo.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a drink, often alcoholic, taken just before going to sleep.

clue.text: Some worship a god, attending temple

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some worshippers praying to a deity while attending a temple.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a tiered tower in East Asia is a kind of Buddhist or Hindu temple.

clue.text: First of games, a home win

indicators.note: first of takes the opening letter of games

parts.note: in means at home

explanation.surface: A sports report: the first match was a home victory.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to win something is to obtain or acquire it.

clue.text: Bird close to old gardening implement

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so the last letter of old

parts.note: a rake is a toothed garden tool

explanation.surface: A bird sitting near a rusty old garden tool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'close to' reads as 'near', but it means the end of 'old'.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a male duck is a kind of bird.

clue.text: Pragmatic type on a roll

parts.note: re means on or about, as in a letter heading
a roll is a list of names

explanation.surface: A practical person enjoying a run of success.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on a roll' reads as an idiom for a winning streak, but each word works separately.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a person who deals with things as they are, practically, is this kind of person.
